disease_label_per_paper: Urinary tract infection presenting with purple urine bag syndrome in a long-term catheterized patient
presentation_summary: 90-year-old woman admitted for acute decompensated heart failure developed urinary retention from constipation during a prolonged inpatient stay.
She was catheterized for symptomatic relief and remained catheterized for about one month.
The initial clue to UTI was purple discoloration of the urinary catheter bag, while the urine in the bag was concentrated brown.
She denied classic urinary symptoms such as dysuria, suprapubic pain, and urgency, but exam showed marked suprapubic tenderness.
Urine sample contained visible sediment/pus; CRP and WBC were elevated.
Urine microscopy/culture later showed Proteus species and pyuria; she improved after catheter removal and ciprofloxacin.

clinical_course: Initial admission was for shortness of breath, wheezing, and worsening peripheral edema from acute decompensated heart failure secondary to myocardial infarction.
During prolonged hospitalization awaiting discharge planning, constipation caused urinary retention and catheterization.
After about one month of catheterization, purple discoloration of the catheter bag prompted reassessment.
A urine sample with visible sediment/pus was sent for microscopy, culture, and sensitivity.
The catheter was removed and empirical ciprofloxacin was started.
After treatment she improved clinically, cognition improved meaningfully, and she was discharged approximately 24 hours later.

outcome.source_text_value: responded well clinically, cognitive status improved, and discharge occurred about 24 hours later

quality_warnings: Proteus species and urine MCS culture result are preserved as non-ranking confirmatory evidence.
This case intentionally retains absent classic urinary symptoms as rankable negative evidence because CAUTI can present atypically in frail catheterized patients.
Purple urine bag discoloration is treated as a device finding within CAUTI context, not as a separate diagnosis label.
